reason: It's MIT and runs in Docker, so if I want it at all I'll have someone stand it up on a spare box over a weekend and pull the parts we like into our own MCP server. I'm not putting a card down for an early preview of something we can self-host or rebuild with a vector DB.
objection: Memory tools rot. Unless it stays current without my engineers tagging owners or writing decisions down somewhere new, the briefings go stale in a month and the agents trust bad context. My engineers won't change how they work to feed another tool.
would_change_my_mind: Running the free self-hosted version on our real repos and Slack for two weeks and seeing it correctly answer 'who owns this service?' and catch an agent change that would have repeated a past incident, with nobody on my team doing extra data entry.
